newsitem.title: USA: King assassin denied tests for liver transplant.
newsitem.headline: King assassin denied tests for liver transplant.

text.p: A judge on Monday turned down a request by James Earl Ray, convicted assassin of civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., for tests that could lead to a life-saving liver transplant.
Ray's lawyer said the ruling was tantamount to a death sentence for the 69-year-old convict, who is dying of liver disease and seeking a trial to prove he was not the killer.

The lawyer, William Pepper, also suggested Monday's decision was part of a continuing cover-up of a conspiracy in the 1968 assassination. He said he would seek a reversal within 10 days in the Tennessee Court of Civil Appeals.

Ray has been near death several times in recent months with terminal liver disease. State officials have said the state does not finance extraordinary medical procedures, such as organ transplants, for prisoners.
Chancery Court Judge Irwin Kilcrease ruled the state's corrections department did not have authority under Tennessee law to allow Ray to travel to another state for a medical evaluation.

Pepper said the University of Pittsburgh Hospital's Transplant Centre was prepared to accept Ray for an evaluation to determine if his age and condition would warrant such surgery, should an organ become available. He said the evaluation and surgery, if they happened, would be financed by private funds which he planned to raise.

One of King's son, Dexter, had urged the court in a letter to allow Ray to have the evaluation. The King family has also backed a trial for Ray, to dispel conspiracy theories that have dogged the tragedy ever since gunshots felled King on the balcony of a Memphis motel 29 years ago.
"Why are they afraid to let this man live? What is it they fear? Why do they have to react in lock step this way when there's nothing the state of Tennessee can lose?" Pepper asked in court.
Without a transplant, Pepper said, Ray will continue to suffer a "lingering death." He quoted Ray's doctor as saying Ray could not survive much longer without a transplant.
Ray confessed to killing King but later denied it and was serving a 99-year sentence.

Tests were conducted last month on the rifle Ray allegedly used, in his bid to win a trial to prove that someone else was the assassin. The test results were due to be released in a Memphis court on June 18 but both Pepper and Ray's brother Jerry told reporters that had been delayed.
Ray's lawyers contend that the rifle found was not the real weapon and that someone else killed King -- perhaps a shadowy figure Ray has identified as "Raoul."
Liver transplants are still somewhat rare, with demand outstripping supply. Drug and alcohol abusers are often denied transplants, though Ray contends that his condition resulted from neither.
